newsitem.title: CANADA: Renaissance sees big '97 production gains.
newsitem.headline: Renaissance sees big '97 production gains.

text.p: Canadian oil and gas driller Renaissance Energy Ltd on Thursday reported big gains in production in 1996 and said it expected the trend to continue in 1997.
Renaissance said oil production for the year grew by 26 percent to 71,921 barrels per day. Natural gas output climbed six percent to 380 million cubic feet per day.

The company said it expected 1997 first-half oil production to average 85,000 barrels per day as winter weather, spring breakup and annual facility maintenance deferred production gains additions until the last six months of the year.
For the full year, oil output was expected to average 92,500 barrels per day, Renaissance said.
The company said it expected gas production in the first quarter of 1997 to average 410 million cubic feet per day.
The full-year average was expected to be 450 million cubic feet per day, but the company called the forecast "somewhat price sensitive."
Renaissance said it acquired a total of 2.5 million acres of land in 1996, increasing its inventory to about 10.6 million acres.
During 1996, the company drilled 1,640 wells in Alberta and Saskatchewan, 895 of which were exploratory, it said.
